Part 0

How to use this pack, and the 10-minute version

Start here. This part tells you what to do this week, which parts to read in the time you have, the fifteen facts that matter most, and how to read the tags and boxes. It includes one diagram that holds the whole story.

Who this is for, and where you are now

This pack is for a UK undergraduate applying for 2027 entry to Deloitte UK's consulting or technology business: a graduate role, a Summer Vacation Scheme (Deloitte's internship) or an Industrial Placement. It assumes you know little about consulting today (about 2 out of 10), that no interview is booked, and that pictures help you learn. It is built only from public sources, each tagged with an ID such as [S14] that you can look up in Part 15.

You are at the application stage, and timing is the most urgent fact in the pack. Deloitte's 2026/27 timeline says Consulting, Advisory, Enabling Functions and Real Estate roles open on 5 October 2026, and Technology roles open partly on 28 September and partly on 5 October [S14] Confirmed. On 4 October only a first wave of Consulting roles was live, in Belfast and Edinburgh [S1] Confirmed. Deloitte runs "a strict one application per year policy" across its early-careers programmes [S14] Confirmed, and it closes roles early when volumes are high [S13][S261] Confirmed. So you get one shot, and an early one is better than a polished late one.

SOURCE UNCERTAIN

Two research passes read the same Deloitte timelines page on the same day and saw different versions: one showed the 2026/27 dates above [S14], the other still showed the 2024 cycle [S262]. Both point to 5 October for Consulting. Treat the date as very likely, and check the board yourself on 5 October.

The 10-minute emergency version

If you read nothing else, read this. Each fact is one you can say out loud, with its source.

£5.81bnDeloitte UK revenue FY26, +2%, UK and Switzerland consolidated [S407]
£1.75bnUK Technology & Transformation revenue FY26, +4% [S407]
US$74.5bnDeloitte global revenue FY26, +3.8% in local currency [S70]
784UK equity partners, a record, up 6.5% [S407]
  1. The year. Deloitte UK's financial year ends on 31 May. In FY26 revenue rose 2% to £5.81bn and distributable profit (the pool shared by the owning partners) rose 14% to £899m [S407] Confirmed.
  2. The precision point. £5.81bn is "UK and Switzerland consolidated" [S407]. Deloitte's metrics split it: UK £5,014m, Switzerland £795m [S88] Confirmed. Say "the UK and Swiss firm" when you quote £5.81bn.
  3. Four businesses. Since 2024 Deloitte runs four businesses. UK FY26: Technology & Transformation £1.75bn (+4%), Tax & Legal £1.36bn (+2%), Audit & Assurance £998m (+3%), Strategy, Risk & Transactions Advisory £913m (+1%). They sum to about £5.01bn, the UK figure [S407][S88] Confirmed.
  4. T&T is your business, and it has had a bumpy ride. It is the largest UK business, about 35% of UK revenue [S88] Inferred. It fell 10% in FY25, then grew 4% in FY26 on ERP, cyber and human capital work [S89][S407] Confirmed.
  5. The global contrast. Globally Deloitte made US$74.5bn, but T&T was the slowest-growing business at 2.5% [S70] Confirmed. In the UK it was the fastest. That contrast is a ready-made question.
  6. The leaders. Darren Graves became UK CEO on 1 June 2026; Jane Whitlock chairs the UK Board; Hayley McKelvey joined the UK Executive as the first Chief AI Officer [S407] Confirmed. Hammad Rafique leads UK T&T [S274] Confirmed.
  7. The EMEA firm. On 1 June 2026 the UK firm joined Deloitte EMEA, led by Richard Houston: 16 firms, about 132,000 people, about €20bn of revenue and over €1.5bn of planned investment over four years [S277][S407] Confirmed.
  8. The independence point. Deloitte also audits. UK rules let an auditor sell only a short "whitelist" of other services to the large listed companies, banks and insurers it audits (public interest entities), with non-audit fees capped at 70% of the audit fee [S39][S364] Confirmed. So consulting is built mostly on clients Deloitte does not audit: £3,819m of non-audit revenue came from non-audit clients in FY25, against £155m from audit clients [S35] Confirmed.
  9. AI inside the firm. Deloitte's own generative AI tool, PairD, reached 75,000 people in Europe and the Middle East by January 2024 [S328], and UK staff sent it about a million prompts a month in FY25 [S85] Confirmed. In October 2025 Deloitte rolled out Anthropic's Claude to more than 470,000 people, with 15,000 to be certified [S116] Confirmed.
  10. AI in your job. The JD's sister posting lists "Using firm-approved AI tools responsibly to support client delivery" as a duty [S3] Confirmed. "Firm-approved" means client data stays inside approved tools.
  11. The Australia lesson. In 2025 Deloitte Australia agreed to repay part of a A$440,000 government contract after its report was found to contain fabricated references and a misquoted court judgment; the revised report disclosed AI use [S388] Confirmed. The lesson: you own every line you send.
  12. The recruitment stages. Application, Immersive Online Assessment, Job Simulation (recorded), Final Stage (a 30 to 40 minute topic discussion and a 50 minute skills and motivation interview), outcome. Each step comes "within four weeks" of the last [S260] Confirmed.
  13. The values. Use the five Shared Values: Lead the way; Serve with integrity; Take care of each other; Foster inclusion; Collaborate for measurable impact [S266] Confirmed. Prep sites still quote an old list of four; do not use it [S264].
  14. Partner numbers, if asked. 784 equity partners is the year-end headcount from the results release; the accounts give 799 on a full-time-equivalent average basis [S407][S88] Confirmed. Quote 784.
  15. The market. UK consulting was worth about £21.8bn in 2025 after 3% growth, with 6% forecast for 2026 [S150] Reported.
SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW (THE 30-SECOND WHY DELOITTE)

"I want to start where the shape of the firm helps me learn. Deloitte keeps audit, tax, advisory and technology in one partnership, and last year showed why that matters: in FY25 T&T revenue fell 10%, but the firm fell only 1% [S89][S305]. That stability pays for £180 million of technology investment and a new Chief AI Officer [S407]. And in FY26 T&T was the fastest-growing UK business, on ERP, cyber and human capital work [S407]. That is the work I want to learn."

ONE QUESTION TO ASK THEM

"Globally T&T grew slowest at 2.5%, but in the UK it grew fastest at 4%. What is the UK doing differently?" [S70][S407]

DON'T SAY THIS

"Deloitte UK made £5.81bn." That figure includes Switzerland [S407]. Also avoid "Deloitte is the biggest consulting firm on every measure": Accenture is about the same size overall [S129].

The master diagram: the firm, the industry and the role on one page

Read Figure 33 from top to bottom. Clients have problems and pay fees (layer 1). Industry forces decide what can be sold, to whom and at what cost (layer 2). Deloitte's model turns that into four businesses, a network, alliances and delivery centres, with an independence wall between audit and the advisory businesses for audit clients (layer 3). Technology & Transformation and its Technology Strategy & Transformation (TST) team are where the JD sits (layer 4). Its ten duties (layer 5) are what you will do, and each one gives you evidence for the four things you say in interview (layer 6).

How to read this pack: tags, sources and boxes

Every non-obvious fact carries a source ID in square brackets, such as [S407]. In the PDF it is a link to the source table in Part 15, which gives the outlet, title, date, web address and whether the page was read in full. A confidence tag follows the claim:

TagWhat it meansExample
ConfirmedA primary source (Deloitte, a regulator, a statute) or two credible outlets agree.UK T&T revenue £1.75bn in FY26 [S407] Confirmed.
ReportedOne credible source, or a primary page that may be out of date. Fine to use; say where it came from.The UK consulting market grew 3% in 2025 [S150] Reported.
InferredThis pack's own reasoning from sourced facts. Present it as your view.T&T is about 35% of UK revenue [S88] Inferred.
EstimateA calculated figure with stated assumptions. Labelled on charts too.UK T&T fee-earning headcount of roughly 5,000 to 7,500 [S23][S24] Estimate.
AnecdoteA candidate's or employee's own account. Useful colour, never proof.An experienced-hire candidate reported a director round [S286] Anecdote.

Coloured boxes mark what to do with a piece of information. Here is one of each.

KEY TERM

Utilisation: the share of a consultant's available hours that is billed to clients. Firms watch it closely because sold hours are revenue.

SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW

A line you can use as written, with its source, for example the 30-second answer above.

DON'T SAY THIS

A common mistake, and why it hurts, for example quoting the old four values [S264].

YOUR OPINION GOES HERE

A debate with both sides and a suggested stance. You choose. Example: should graduates fear AI? Part 8 gives the case each way.

SOURCE UNCERTAIN

Sources disagree or the fact rests on one weak source. Example: the opening-date page above. Part 16 lists every case.

Figures have numbered titles that state the point, and a caption naming the sources and dates. Scenario cards in Part 11 are coloured green, amber or red for easy, medium and hard.

Part 1

The role, decoded line by line, and the team mapped

What the job actually is, in plain English: the posting quoted, every duty translated into what you would do on a Tuesday, who you would work with, the rules that fence the work in, and a map of the team you would join, with each box marked by how sure we are.

Read this first: timing, and which posting is "the JD"

You are researching on 4 October 2026. That date matters, because Deloitte UK opens most of its 2027 consulting roles the next day. Its official timeline says Consulting, Advisory, Enabling Functions and Real Estate open on "5th October". Technology opened partly on 28 September and partly opens on 5 October. Scotland opened first, on 21 September [S14] Confirmed.

5 Oct 2026Consulting and Advisory early-careers roles open [S14]
23 Oct 2026Closing date for THE JD (Belfast TST graduate, 25060); may close earlier [S2]
168Early-careers programmes live on 4 Oct 2026, mostly Audit, Tax and IT Audit [S1]
1Applications allowed per year across all Deloitte UK early-careers roles [S14]
SOURCE UNCERTAIN: WHICH POSTING, AND WHEN

The JD used in this pack is a Belfast posting, not a London one. On 4 October 2026 the live board showed a first wave of Consulting roles in Belfast and Edinburgh only. London Consulting graduate postings were not yet live [S1] Confirmed. This pack therefore treats "Technology Strategy Consulting - Technology Strategy & Transformation", Full Time Graduate, Belfast, posting 25060, as THE JD [S2] Confirmed. It was chosen because it is a full graduate role, it sits in the core technology consulting model, and its duty list is the most general on the board.

What to do: re-check the board on 5 October. When the London Technology & Transformation postings appear, compare their text line by line with the extract below. Deloitte says roles "may close before the deadline if we experience high demand" [S2], so apply early once you have chosen.

The one-application rule. Deloitte runs "a strict one application per year policy across our Early Careers opportunities" [S14] Confirmed. Choosing the team is a real decision. Read the sister postings table later in this Part before you pick.

Two oddities in THE JD. Its header says "This role sits within the Finance Transformation Consulting persona", and it says there are "two core areas" but describes only one [S2] Confirmed (that the text says this). Both look like copy-and-paste leftovers from a template Inferred. Do not build an answer on either line.

The job is a graduate role starting in September 2027. You need a 2:1 (obtained or predicted) in any subject and must have graduated by September 2027 [S2] Confirmed. The salary is not stated. The posting says it is below the threshold for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship, so Deloitte cannot progress candidates who need that visa [S2] Confirmed. Self-reported salary snippets of about £34k to £39k exist for consulting graduates, but they are low-confidence and should not be quoted in an interview [S58][S59] Reported.

What Deloitte calls things now

Deloitte renamed its businesses in recent years, and older blog posts use the old names. Getting the current names right is an easy signal that you have done your reading. Here is the vocabulary, from the top down.

Four businesses

Deloitte UK runs four businesses. Each is a large division with its own leaders, people and revenue line [S24][S23] Confirmed:

Business (firm name)What students seeUK revenue FY26What it does, in one line
Technology & Transformation (T&T)"Consulting"£1,746m (+4%)Designs and delivers change in how clients run, mostly through technology: strategy through to implementation and managed services [S12][S40].
Strategy, Risk & Transactions Advisory (SR&T)"Advisory"£913m (+1%)Strategy (including Monitor Deloitte), mergers and acquisitions, valuations, infrastructure, sustainability, and risk, regulatory and forensic work [S15][S45].
Tax & LegalTax & Legal£1,357m (+2%)Tax advice and compliance, and legal services.
Audit & AssuranceAudit & Assurance£998m (+3%)Statutory audit (checking companies' accounts) and other assurance.

Revenue: UK only, year to 31 May 2026 [S23] Confirmed. The headline £5.81bn in press reports is "UK and Switzerland consolidated"; UK alone was £5,014m and Switzerland £795m [S407][S88] Confirmed.

T&T is the largest UK business. It earned about 35% of UK revenue in FY26 Inferred (arithmetic on [S23]). It fell about 10% in FY25 and grew 4% in FY26, but is still below its FY24 level of £1,857m [S23] Confirmed (figures). Trade press named ERP implementation (large finance and operations software) and cyber as material contributors to the FY26 growth [S30] Reported.

KEY TERM

"Consulting" versus "Advisory": on the early-careers website, "Consulting" is the label for teams inside Technology & Transformation, and "Advisory" is the label for teams inside Strategy, Risk & Transactions [S12][S15][S57] Confirmed. Deloitte's own results footnote says its "advisory businesses include the Technology & Transformation (T&T) business as well as the Strategy, Risk & Transactions Advisory (SRTA) business" [S407] Confirmed. So the press may call both "advisory". In interviews, use the business names.

Offerings: the teams inside a business

Each business is split into offerings. An offering is a team that owns a type of service: its methods, its software partnerships and its people. Inside T&T, Deloitte UK's website lists these offerings [S12][S40] Confirmed:

  • Customer (Deloitte Digital): marketing, commerce, sales and service technology, such as customer relationship management systems.
  • Cyber: security strategy, defence and resilience, digital trust and privacy, and managed cyber operations.
  • Engineering, AI & Data (EAD): software engineering, data platforms and AI, plus Operations, Industry & Domain Solutions.
  • Enterprise Technology & Performance (ET&P): the big "back-office" platforms and the strategy around them. It includes Finance Transformation, SAP, Oracle, ServiceNow, Supply Chain & Network Operations, and Technology Strategy & Transformation (TST), the team in THE JD.
  • Human Capital: HR strategy, workforce and organisation change, HR systems, Major Programmes, and actuarial work.
KEY TERM

Persona: a recruiting family Deloitte uses to group early-careers roles by type of work. The current consulting personas are Business Transformation Consulting, Enterprise Applications Consulting, Technology Strategy Consulting, Finance Transformation Consulting and Risk & Controls Consulting [S2][S4][S7][S8][S9][S10] Confirmed. A persona tells you the kind of work. The team name after the dash tells you which offering you land in. "Technology Strategy Consulting - Technology Strategy & Transformation" means persona first, team second.

KEY TERM

Industry: the client sector a team serves. Deloitte UK's industries are Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Healthcare; Technology, Media & Telecommunications; plus Private Equity [S12][S26] Confirmed. Offerings (what you do) and industries (who you do it for) cross like the rows and columns of a grid. That grid is called a matrix, and it decides who you work with.

KEY TERM

Engagement: one piece of paid client work with an agreed scope, team, price and end date. Consultants say "project" and "engagement" interchangeably. Analyst: Deloitte's name for a graduate joiner in T&T ("As a Graduate (we call you Analysts)") [S4] Confirmed.

Two older names have faded. "Strategy & Operations" no longer appears as an early-careers team name. "Government & Public Services" now appears as an industry, and "Defence & Security" appears inside many experienced-hire job titles [S40][S49] Confirmed. If an older blog says "Deloitte Consulting has five service lines", it predates the four-business model.

What the firm is hiring for right now

Job postings are one of the few public windows into a private partnership. On 4 October 2026 Deloitte UK listed 591 experienced-hire postings. We parsed 551 of them and counted them by business and city [S49]. Figure 14 shows the result. Treat it as a sample: 40 postings could not be read, and a posting is a vacancy, not a person.

Two readings matter. First, T&T is where the hiring is: just over half of all parsed experienced postings [S49] Confirmed (our count). That shows where the firm is investing, not that T&T is half the firm. Second, London is the main T&T hub, but Manchester is a strong second, and Bristol, Belfast, Edinburgh and Glasgow all hire into T&T [S49] Confirmed (count) Inferred (reading). If a London interviewer asks whether you would work with colleagues in other cities, the honest answer is that you almost certainly will.

THE JD: the text that matters

Below is a compact extract of THE JD, keeping every duty line word for word. Navigation text, benefits links and the application small print are left out. The full text was read on 4 October 2026 [S2] Confirmed.

Technology Strategy Consulting - Technology Strategy & Transformation
Programme: Full Time Graduate. Career Path: Consulting. Location: Belfast. Start Date: September-2027. Posting 25060. Closes 23 October 2026.

What does this team do? "In Technology Strategy and Transformation (TST), we focus on enabling our clients to be the best that they can be. We work with their most senior leaders and top-level executives to help them digitise and modernise their organisations from the ground up. We lead the transformation of the organisation itself with innovative and core technologies, helping organisations move away from IT, the department of computers, to technology as a business partner and enabler.

Our teams combine strategic thinking, advisory services, and cutting-edge technology capabilities to create a digital core that has the capability to drive new processes, improved analytics, and improved performance across the business.

We proudly partner with some of the world's largest and most successful organisations, helping COOs, CFOs, CIOs, and their teams achieve their goals, whether that is improving financial performance, accelerating speed to market, delivering continuous innovation, and entering exciting new fields like AI. ... We help them to transform how their businesses run and the technologies they use in ways that drive net zero and incorporate inclusive ways of working.

Our TST market offerings include: Technology Operating Model; Enterprise Transformation & Agility; Technology Strategy, Vision and Architecture; Technology Sourcing & Commercial Management."

What kind of work will I do? "As a Full Time Graduate in TST, you will work on large-scale technology transformations, from the design through to implementation. As part of your role, you will be:

  • Learning how to engage with clients to solve their most complex problems
  • Working with individuals from our clients' business and IT teams to understand what the problems and needs are, and transforming those into technical requirements
  • Creating documents crucial to the delivery and execution of the programme, alongside materials presented back to clients
  • Discovering how technologies support everything an organisation does, and which technologies work best for each part of a business
  • Using firm-approved AI tools responsibly to support client delivery
  • Help assess technology investments, identify opportunities to improve value, agility, efficiency, and user experience.

Throughout your time at Deloitte, you will be working with teams across our wider Technology and Transformation practice, understanding how we bring our range of technical expertise and combine them in the way that best serves our clients."

How will I develop? "... What technologies organisations currently use and how they can transform those to better achieve their strategic objectives; How to interpret business strategic and objectives and transform those into requirements and solutions; What large-scale technology transformations look like; How to build rapport with clients and ensure they have confidence in your capability."

Also in the posting: minimum 2:1 in any discipline; hybrid working, with client-facing staff "expected to attend client sites on certain days"; final assessment and induction in person; one application per year; no Skilled Worker sponsorship [S2].

The JD decoded, line by line

The JD's lines collapse into ten duties, labelled D1 to D10. The same labels are used in the scenario playbook later in the pack, so you can trace any practice scenario back to a line of the posting. Each duty below has five parts: what it means day to day, who you deal with, the tools, what good looks like, and what the line reveals about the firm.

A word on confidence. Deloitte does not publish an analyst's diary. The "day to day" content is built from Deloitte's own job postings, staff profiles and service pages, and is marked Inferred where it is our reasoning. Quotes are from the postings themselves.

Figure 15 first shows where these duties sit in the life of a client problem. Most engagements move through some or all of seven stages. Your contribution changes at each one.

D1. Senior client engagement and rapport

"We work with their most senior leaders and top-level executives"; "How to build rapport with clients and ensure they have confidence in your capability" [S2]

Day to dayYou will rarely lead a conversation with a client's chief information officer (CIO) in year one. You prepare the pack the partner or director uses, sit in the room, take notes and chase the actions afterwards. Rapport at your level is built in small exchanges with the client's analysts and managers: answering a data question the same day, sending minutes within hours Inferred.
Who you deal withClient: CIO, chief financial officer (CFO), chief operating officer (COO) and their direct reports. Deloitte: a partner who owns the relationship, a director or associate director who leads the engagement, a manager who runs the plan day to day Inferred (grade names Confirmed [S49][S66]).
ToolsPowerPoint meeting packs, Word minutes, Excel action logs, Microsoft Teams Inferred.
What good looks likeReliability. Small promises kept. You know the client's organisation chart and who decides what. You never surprise your manager Inferred.
What it revealsTST sells to the top of the client. Its strategy work can open the door to larger implementation work elsewhere in T&T Inferred. A T&T director describes a week with "a check-in with my client on a project, so we can manage any potential risks" and "preparing a bid to win new work" [S55] Confirmed (quote).

D2. The IT operating model

"helping organisations move away from IT, the department of computers, to technology as a business partner and enabler" [S2]

KEY TERM

Operating model: how a function is organised, staffed, funded, sourced (in-house or outsourced) and governed. A technology operating model answers "who does what in technology, who pays, and who decides". It is the first of TST's four market offerings [S2] Confirmed.

Day to dayCurrent-state interviews with IT leaders; a capability map (a one-page grid of everything the IT function does); an IT cost baseline in Excel; summaries of supplier contracts; organisation charts in PowerPoint Inferred.
Who you deal withThe CIO's leadership team, finance business partners who hold the IT cost data, procurement teams who hold the contracts Inferred.
ToolsExcel for cost baselines and contract summaries, PowerPoint for maps and charts Inferred.
What good looks likeA baseline that the client's finance team agrees with. If the starting numbers are disputed, every later recommendation is disputed too Inferred.
What it reveals"Technology Sourcing & Commercial Management" is another TST offering [S2] Confirmed. Sourcing work (deciding what to outsource, to whom, on what contract) means TST analysts read contracts and compare suppliers Inferred. The old view of IT as a cost centre is what TST is paid to change.

D3. The digital core and the technology landscape

"create a digital core"; "Discovering how technologies support everything an organisation does, and which technologies work best for each part of a business" [S2]

KEY TERM

ERP (enterprise resource planning): one large software system that runs a company's core processes, such as finance, purchasing, supply chain and often HR. SAP and Oracle are the best-known vendors. The digital core is the ERP plus the other core platforms and data that everything else hangs off Inferred (from [S12][S40]).

Day to dayApplication inventories (a list of every system the client runs, with owner, cost and age); "keep, retire or replace" assessments; vendor comparisons Inferred.
Who you deal withEnterprise architects on both sides; Deloitte's platform teams for SAP, Oracle, Workday or ServiceNow Inferred.
ToolsExcel inventories, architecture diagrams, vendor documentation Inferred. Deloitte UK lists alliances with Adobe, Anaplan, Apple, AWS, Google, Informatica, MuleSoft, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, UiPath, Workday and Workiva [S12][S40] Confirmed.
What good looks likeYou can explain in two sentences what each major system does and who depends on it Inferred.
What it revealsDeloitte is both adviser and implementer. One posting claims "We are the number one global SAP delivery partner with over 200 implementations delivered to date" [S52] Reported (Deloitte's own claim). That raises a fair question: can an adviser with large software alliances recommend platforms objectively? Have a view ready Inferred.

D4. The business case and value

"improving financial performance, accelerating speed to market, delivering continuous innovation, and entering exciting new fields like AI"; "Help assess technology investments, identify opportunities to improve value, agility, efficiency, and user experience" [S2]

KEY TERM

Business case: the document that justifies spending money on a change. It sets out costs, benefits, risks, timing and options, and usually a payback period (how long until the benefits repay the cost). Boards approve large technology programmes on the strength of it.

Day to dayBenchmarking IT spend against peers, application portfolio rationalisation, cost and benefit models in Excel, sensitivity tables ("what if the benefits arrive a year late?") Inferred. Deloitte UK's TST service page uses the same words as the JD: "increase the value, agility, efficiency and experience of technology investments" [S41] Confirmed.
Who you deal withThe CFO's team and finance business partners, who will challenge every number Inferred.
ToolsExcel models; benchmark data; PowerPoint summaries Inferred.
What good looks likeEvery number traces to a source. Assumptions are written down and agreed. Each benefit has a named owner on the client side Inferred.
What it revealsThe business case is the product. Clients spend millions only when someone shows the benefit. An analyst comfortable with Excel and basic finance is useful from week one Inferred.

D5. Net zero and inclusive ways of working

"transforming their enterprises to make advances in sustainability and diversity and inclusion ... in ways that drive net zero and incorporate inclusive ways of working" [S2]

Day to dayLow daily weight for an Analyst. You might add an emissions line to a cloud migration case, or check that a new system works for users with accessibility needs Inferred.
Who you deal withThe client's sustainability lead; Deloitte's Sustainability team, which sits in SR&T [S15] Confirmed (that it sits there).
ToolsThe same business case models, with sustainability measures added Inferred.
What good looks likeYou can define net zero (cutting greenhouse gas emissions as far as possible and balancing the rest) and name one technology lever, such as retiring old data centres Inferred.
What it revealsDeloitte wants people who connect technology to wider outcomes. It is also fertile ground for an opinion: where do technology and sustainability goals pull against each other, for example the energy demand of AI computing? Inferred

D6. Large-scale transformation, design through implementation

"you will work on large-scale technology transformations, from the design through to implementation" [S2]

KEY TERM

PMO (programme management office): the small team that keeps a large programme organised: plans, status reports, risks, budgets, governance meetings. RAID log: a running list of Risks, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies, each with an owner and a date. Juniors often own the RAID log. Steering committee: the senior client and Deloitte group that meets regularly to take programme decisions.

Day to dayMost first-year time on large programmes goes to PMO work: RAID logs, status reports, plan updates, meeting packs, requirement logs and test tracking Inferred. Sister postings say it openly: "scheduling meetings and taking minutes, tracking deadlines, and preparing materials" (Cyber) [S9] and "materials for workshops, communications, project plans and progress reporting" (Customer Products) [S4] Confirmed.
Who you deal withThe client programme director and workstream leads; your Deloitte manager; build teams on and offshore. An SAP posting asks for communication "with clients and colleagues both on and offshore" [S51]; a Workday posting mentions "engineering teams (onshore and offshore)" [S50] Confirmed.
ToolsExcel, PowerPoint, Word, Jira or Azure DevOps for work tracking, Microsoft Teams Inferred. Deloitte UK advertises an "Atlassian Center of Excellence" (Atlassian makes Jira) [S49] Confirmed.
What good looks likeThe RAID log is current, every action has an owner and a date, and the status report tells the truth even when the news is bad Inferred.
What it revealsDeloitte sells the whole lifecycle, from the first strategy conversation to running the system afterwards. That is its pitch against pure strategy firms on one side and pure IT outsourcers on the other Inferred.

The design-to-implementation span is why the same Analyst can have very different years. Figure 16 contrasts the two channels of work you could be staffed on.

D7. Requirements

"Working with individuals from our clients' business and IT teams to understand what the problems and needs are, and transforming those into technical requirements" [S2]

KEY TERM

Requirement: a precise, testable statement of what a system or process must do. "A manager must be able to approve expenses under £500 from a phone" is a requirement. "Make expenses easier" is not. A user story is a requirement written from the user's point of view: "As a manager, I want to ... so that ...".

Day to dayRun or support workshops; capture "as-is" processes (how work is done today); write requirements or user stories; map them to what the software can do Inferred. Finance Transformation describes "Getting to the bottom of client's problems through interactive workshops and labs" [S8] Confirmed.
Who you deal withClient process owners (for example the head of accounts payable), client IT, Deloitte functional and technical leads Inferred.
ToolsProcess maps, requirements trackers in Excel or Jira, workshop templates Inferred.
What good looks likeRequirements that are testable, traced to a business objective and signed off by a named client owner Inferred.
What it revealsTST is not purely strategy. Its graduates translate between business and technology people, which is the scarce skill on most programmes Inferred.

D8. Documents and client materials

"Creating documents crucial to the delivery and execution of the programme, alongside materials presented back to clients" [S2]

Day to dayPowerPoint is the main output: steering committee packs, design documents, playbooks, training material Inferred.
Who you deal withYour manager, who reviews; the client audience, who decides Inferred.
ToolsPowerPoint and Word in Deloitte templates, with Excel behind every chart Inferred.
What good looks likeOne message per slide, stated in the title. Numbers that tie to a source. No typos. Expect several rounds of review on early drafts Inferred.
What it revealsClear writing is a core skill. The final-stage topic discussion and interview test the same thing: a clear point backed by evidence [S17] Confirmed (format).

D9. Firm-approved AI tools, used responsibly

"Using firm-approved AI tools responsibly to support client delivery" [S3][S2]

Day to daySummarising long documents, drafting first versions of minutes or slides, desk research, checking spreadsheets Inferred. Deloitte's audit business uses an internal tool, PairD, to "analyse, summarise, explain, and translate confidential data, all within its secure digital ecosystem" [S345] Confirmed. The names of T&T's internal tools could not be confirmed (gap).
Who you deal withYour manager, who will want to know what you used AI for; the firm's AI governance, which covers "use-case approval" and "data governance" [S345] Confirmed.
ToolsOnly tools the firm has approved and secured. Never a public chatbot for client material Inferred (from [S36][S345]).
What good looks likeYou check every fact, number and citation an AI tool produces before it reaches a client. A Deloitte article puts it plainly: "accountability is squarely a human domain" [S347] Confirmed.
What it revealsAI use is now a written junior duty. Deloitte UK named its first Chief AI Officer, Hayley McKelvey, from 1 June 2026 [S407][S274] Confirmed. The cautionary tale: Deloitte Australia agreed in 2025 to repay part of a fee after an AI-assisted report contained references that did not exist [S388] Confirmed.

D10. Teaming across the wider Technology & Transformation practice

"you will be working with teams across our wider Technology and Transformation practice, understanding how we bring our range of technical expertise and combine them in the way that best serves our clients" [S2]

Day to dayJoining a programme led by another offering (say the SAP team), alongside cyber, data and change colleagues; working with Belfast or offshore build teams Inferred (from [S21][S50][S51]).
Who you deal withYour People Leader (development and career) and your Resource Manager (who allocates you to engagements) [S4] Confirmed (titles; their roles are inferred from the titles).
ToolsInternal staffing and directory systems; names not public Inferred.
What good looks likeSeveral teams know you as useful. That gives you more choice of engagements Inferred.
What it revealsDeloitte's pitch is breadth: strategy, platforms, cyber, data and people change from one firm. A Major Programmes posting says "we collaborate with other geographies and member firms on high-profile engagements" [S53] Confirmed.

YOUR OPINION GOES HERE

Prompt: TST or an implementation team such as HR Applications? For TST: broader exposure, senior clients, business-case skills that transfer anywhere. For an implementation team: a certifiable technical skill early, clearer daily output, strong demand for platform skills. Suggested stance: pick the one whose daily tasks you would enjoy in month three, not the one with the grander title, and say why in one sentence.

Two worked days in the seat

These two days are illustrations, not diaries. They are built from Deloitte's own duty lists [S2][S4][S8][S9][S6], from a T&T director's and a T&T senior manager's described weeks [S55][S56], and from the hybrid working note in THE JD [S2]. No first-hand analyst diaries could be read, because review sites blocked access. Every time and task below is Inferred.

SOURCE UNCERTAIN

Working hours, travel frequency and how often analysts work late are not published by Deloitte. Treat the times as a sketch of the rhythm, not a promise or a warning.

Day A: a technology operating model review (advisory)

The client is a retailer whose board thinks its IT function is too expensive and too slow. Deloitte has been hired for eight weeks to describe today's IT function and propose a better one. You are the Analyst on a team of four.

TimeWhat you doWhy it matters
08:30Travel to the client's head office. Client-facing staff "might be expected to attend client sites on certain days" [S2].Being on site builds trust and gets you answers faster.
09:00Team stand-up with your manager and two consultants. Your actions: finish interview notes, update the IT cost baseline.You leave knowing exactly what "done" means today.
09:30Sit in on an interview with the Head of Infrastructure. A senior consultant leads; you take notes.Your notes become the evidence base for the recommendations.
10:30Write up notes into the interview log and tag themes (sourcing, skills, cloud costs).Tagging lets the team see patterns across 20 interviews.
11:30Excel: reconcile IT spend from the client's finance team against supplier contracts. Flag gaps to the manager.D2 and D4: the baseline must survive the CFO's challenge.
13:00Lunch with the team.
13:45Build two slides for Thursday's steering committee: "current state on one page" and "cost by capability".D8: the slides carry the team's message to the decision makers.
15:00Manager reviews the slides. You rework them.Expect red pen. It is how quality is built, not a judgement on you.
16:00Desk research on peer benchmarks, using firm-approved tools [S2]. Save every source.D9: the AI output is a draft; you own the facts.
17:00Update the RAID log; send minutes from the morning interview.Same-day minutes are a quiet signal of reliability.
17:45Record today's hours against the engagement code. Accurate time recording is a Global Code commitment [S36].Fees and integrity both depend on it.
18:00Finish slides if comments arrived late. Days run longer near deadlines.

Day B: an HR or finance system rollout (delivery)

The client is a large organisation replacing its HR system with Workday, or its finance system with SAP. The programme has run for a year and has 18 months to go. You are one of several Analysts in a workstream.

TimeWhat you doWhy it matters
08:45Daily stand-up for your workstream: client process owner, Deloitte functional lead, offshore build team on the call.D10: the matrix in one meeting.
09:15Update the requirements tracker in Jira or Excel after yesterday's design workshop.D7: a requirement not logged is a requirement lost.
10:00Support a design workshop. You run the screen and capture decisions and open questions. Finance Transformation calls these "interactive workshops and labs" [S8].Decisions recorded today stop arguments in six months.
11:30Configure or test a simple element in the test system, with guidance. HR Applications Analysts "configure the chosen HR application" [S6].Hands-on skill, and the first step to certification.
13:00Lunch.
13:45Write test scripts for user acceptance testing (UAT).Business users, not the build team, sign off UAT.
15:00Defect triage call: log defects, assign owners, chase fixes with the build team.D6: problems get owners and dates.
16:00Prepare the weekly status report for the PMO.Status that tells the truth protects the client and the firm.
17:00Data migration reconciliation in Excel: do record counts in the old and new systems match?Bad data at go-live is the most common visible failure.
17:45Timesheet; plan tomorrow. Go-live weeks are longer and can include weekend cutover support.
KEY TERM

UAT (user acceptance testing): the stage where real business users test a new system against agreed requirements and decide whether to accept it. Cutover: the planned switch from the old system to the new one, often over a weekend. Defect: anything that does not work as the requirement says.

Figure 17 puts the two days side by side. The colour shows the type of work. Notice how much of each day is documents and coordination, and how little is the dramatic "presenting to the board" picture of consulting.

Kinds of work, grades, and how people are judged

A taxonomy of consulting activity

Almost all T&T work fits into eleven activity types. The order roughly follows the life of a client relationship. The labels are ours Inferred; the evidence that each exists at Deloitte UK is cited.

Activity typeWhat it is and the usual formatsEvidence it exists at Deloitte UK
1. Business development and bidsProposals, pricing, "orals" (pitch meetings), credentials packs.A director's week includes "preparing a bid to win new work" [S55]; HR Applications Analysts may work on "bids for new client opportunities" [S6]; the board lists a "Bid Advisor" and a "Pricing Manager, Technology and Transformation" [S49].
2. Discovery and current stateInterviews, data requests, process maps, system inventories.Requirements and problem-finding duties in THE JD [S2] and Finance Transformation [S8].
3. Strategy and optionsTarget operating model, sourcing strategy, roadmap, architecture.TST's four market offerings [S2].
4. Business caseCosts, benefits, risks, payback; later, value tracking."Help assess technology investments" [S2]; TST service page [S41].
5. DesignFuture-state processes and systems; requirements; workshops and "labs"."Designing the future state of a finance function" [S8].
6. Build, configure, integrateSetting up SAP, Oracle, Workday, Salesforce, ServiceNow; cloud and data engineering.Offerings and postings [S6][S12][S49].
7. TestingTest scripts, UAT, quality engineering.Quality engineering roles on the board [S49].
8. Deployment and cutoverGo-live planning, data migration, cutover weekends.Implementation duties in platform postings [S50][S51] Inferred (detail).
9. Programme management (PMO)Plans, RAID logs, status reports, steering committees."Major Programmes" is a named Human Capital team [S5][S40]; junior PMO tasks in [S9].
10. Change, training and adoptionCommunications, training, stakeholder support.The Transformation Activation change team [S5].
11. Managed services ("Operate")Running a system or process for the client over years.ET&P, EAD, Human Capital and Cyber each list an "as a Service" or "Operate" line [S12]; Customer Products sells "multi-year ... operate services" [S4].

The common formats you will meet: the stakeholder interview (one client leader, 45 to 60 minutes, notes afterwards); the workshop (a group of client staff working through a process or decision, with Deloitte facilitating); the steering committee (senior decision meeting, usually monthly); the daily stand-up (15 minutes, what each person did and is doing next); the status report (weekly, one or two pages); and the orals (the pitch meeting before a client chooses a firm) Inferred. A T&T senior manager describes a client workshop "where we try and work out what they need for a new project. We show them examples of our previous work and talk to them about the needs of their customers" [S56] Confirmed (quote).

Grades, and what each is judged on

Deloitte UK's grade names are confirmed from its job titles, staff profiles and pay report [S4][S49][S66][S25]. What each grade is judged on is not published. The right-hand column is the usual pattern in large professional services firms and is Inferred.

GradeTypical role on an engagementJudged mainly on (Inferred)
Analyst (graduate entry)Notes, analysis, slides, trackers, testing support.Accuracy, speed, reliability, learning, attitude.
ConsultantOwns a piece of a workstream; client-facing at working level.Ownership, client trust, quality without heavy review.
Senior ConsultantRuns a small workstream; coaches analysts.Delivery of the workstream, coaching, judgement.
ManagerRuns the engagement day to day: plan, budget, team, quality.Delivery on time and budget, client relationship at working level, team health.
Senior Manager / Associate DirectorSeveral workstreams or engagements; shapes extensions.Selling follow-on work, managing risk, building the practice.
DirectorLeads engagements and client relationships; bids.Sales, client relationships, quality and risk.
Partner (salaried or equity)Owns client relationships and the engagement's risk.For equity partners Deloitte says profit share follows "quality, risk, performance, and leadership" [S93] Confirmed.
KEY TERM

Utilisation: the share of your available working hours that is charged to clients. Chargeable hours are recorded against a client engagement code; non-chargeable hours go to training, internal work or bids. Juniors usually carry the highest utilisation expectations Inferred. Deloitte UK does not publish its targets (gap). Its accounts say even fixed-fee revenue is measured "based on the actual inputs of time at charge-out rates, via timesheet reporting" [S93] Confirmed, which is why the timesheet matters so much.

What the team is judged on

Deloitte does not publish targets for individual offerings. What is visible is the business line. UK T&T revenue was £1,857m in FY24, £1,675m in FY25 and £1,746m in FY26 [S23] Confirmed. Global T&T grew 2.5% in local currency in FY26, the slowest of Deloitte's four global businesses [S34] Confirmed, so the UK practice grew faster than the network average that year Inferred. The FY26 recovery was credited to work including ERP implementation and cyber [S30] Reported.

From the firm's own reporting, a T&T team is likely judged on: revenue growth and sales pipeline; profitability, which depends on utilisation, pricing and keeping fixed-fee work on budget; quality and risk (no failed programmes, no independence breaches); and people measures such as retention and promotions Inferred (from [S93][S94]). The firm rates its reputation and "Client Portfolio" risks highly, citing "Increasing breadth and depth of non-audit offerings (including Operate)" as a threat [S94] Confirmed.

Career path: what is sourced, and what is not

  • Start. Graduates join an in-person "Analyst Induction Programme (AIP)", then business-area training "for a few more weeks", supported by a "Consulting Early Experience team" and early-talent sponsors [S4] Confirmed.
  • Two named people. Each joiner meets a "People Leader and Resource Manager" [S4] Confirmed. From the titles, the People Leader looks after development and the Resource Manager allocates you to engagements Inferred.
  • Qualifications. "The professional qualification pathway is determined by the business area that your role is in." Options listed for Consulting graduates include an MSc in Digital and Business Risk Management, the CIMA Certificate in Business Accounting (with the option to complete full CIMA), and an actuarial qualification [S18] Confirmed. Platform certifications appear in postings, such as becoming "a certified implementation practitioner" [S6] Confirmed.
  • Promotion. Promotions are "given on merit" and pay and promotions are reviewed annually [S19] Confirmed. In 2026 over 6,000 people were promoted, from a firm of about 25,000 [S25][S407] Confirmed. Average in-grade salary rose 4.2% for FY27 and the bonus pool rose 14% [S25] Confirmed.
  • Partnership. 48 people became partners in 2026, of whom 15 were in T&T, the largest share [S25] Confirmed.
  • Not found (gaps). Typical years per grade; graduate salary; the name of the current performance management system; utilisation targets. A common market pattern is one to three years per grade below Manager, but this is Inferred and unverified. Do not quote numbers for these in an interview.

The compliance and control side of the job

Consulting at Deloitte comes with rules that do not exist at a pure consultancy. The reason is structural. Deloitte is also one of the UK's largest auditors, and an auditor must be independent of the companies it audits. That one fact shapes which clients T&T can serve, what you may own personally, and how a new engagement starts. Four other controls apply to everyone: conflicts, confidentiality, approved AI and honest timesheets.

Independence: why an audit firm's consultants have extra rules

KEY TERM

Independence: the requirement that an auditor be free of interests that could bias its audit opinion, and be seen to be free of them. Public interest entity (PIE): broadly, a listed company, bank or insurer, where the public relies heavily on the audited accounts. The rules for PIE audit clients are the strictest.

  • The standard. The UK auditing regulator, the Financial Reporting Council (FRC), sets the Revised Ethical Standard 2024, effective 15 December 2024 [S38] Confirmed.
  • The whitelist for PIEs. For PIE audit clients, an audit firm "and, where the audit firm belongs to a network, any member of such network, shall not provide (either directly or indirectly) to the audited entity ... services other than those set out" in a permitted list, subject to audit committee approval [S39] (para 5.40) Confirmed. Prohibited services include "designing and implementing financial information technology systems" and playing "any part in the management or decision-making of the audited entity" [S364] Confirmed. In plain English: Deloitte consulting cannot sell most technology implementation to a listed company that Deloitte audits.
  • The fee cap. Non-audit fees for a PIE are capped at 70% of the average audit fee of the last three years [S39][S364] Confirmed.
  • The management threat. Any service where a reasonable third party would conclude the firm is taking "a management role" for an audit-relevant entity is prohibited [S364] Confirmed. If a client that Deloitte audits says "just approve it for us", that is an escalation, not a favour Inferred.
  • Personal independence. Partners and those closely associated must not hold a financial interest (other than an immaterial indirect one) in an entity relevant to an engagement of the firm [S39] (para 2.3); people on or able to influence an engagement have the same restriction [S39] (para 2.4) Confirmed. New joiners must "clear Personal Independence checks before you join us" [S261] Confirmed. Practically, expect to declare investments and to check a restricted list before buying individual shares Inferred.
£3,819mFY25 non-audit revenue from entities Deloitte UK does not audit [S35]
£155mFY25 non-audit revenue from entities it does audit [S35]
~96%Share of non-audit revenue from non-audit clients (Inferred arithmetic)
32Engagements referred to the Public Interest Review Group in FY25 [S35]

The two revenue numbers are the clearest picture of how independence shapes the business. In FY25 Deloitte UK earned £155m from non-audit services to entities it audits, against £3,819m from non-audit services to entities it does not audit [S35] Confirmed. About 96% of consulting, tax and advisory revenue therefore comes from clients the firm does not audit Inferred. The consulting business is built on a client list largely separate from the audit client list.

Conflict checks before any engagement

"All proposed engagements and business and financial relationships go through a conflict check before they are accepted." Where conflicts cannot be reduced to an acceptable level, "we decline the engagement" [S35] Confirmed. Engagements with high public-interest or reputational risk go to the Public Interest Review Group (PIRG): 32 matters in FY25, of which 9% were declined [S35][S345] Confirmed. For T&T and SR&T the firm set up a "Consultative Forum" and a "globally aligned client portfolio management process" [S94] Confirmed. A global acceptance and continuance platform is planned for UK implementation in FY2027 [S35] Confirmed. As an Analyst you will not run these checks, but you may be asked to declare your own conflicts, and you should never start work before the engagement is formally accepted Inferred.

Confidentiality between clients

Deloitte's Global Principles of Business Conduct say: "We prohibit disclosure of confidential and personal information entrusted to us unless granted permission or there is a legal or professional right or duty to disclose", and "We prohibit the use of confidential information about our clients for personal advantage or for the benefit of third parties" [S36] Confirmed. A consultant may work for two competitors in the same year. What you learn at one must never reach the other. The PwC Australia tax leaks scandal of 2023, in which confidential government information was used to win clients, shows the cost when this fails [S392] Confirmed.

Government work adds another layer. Many T&T roles prefer or require UK security clearance: "preference will be for those who have SC clearance or eligibility to obtain SC Clearance" [S54] Confirmed. Graduates placed on public sector work may be asked to apply Inferred.

Inside information on deal work

Some T&T work touches listed companies or deals, for example integration planning before an acquisition is announced. UK market abuse law defines inside information as precise, non-public information that would be likely to have a significant effect on prices if made public [S358] Confirmed. Disclosure is lawful only "in the normal exercise of an employment, a profession or duties" [S359] Confirmed, and insider dealing, tipping and unlawful disclosure are prohibited [S360] Confirmed. In practice: do not trade, do not tip, and do not discuss the work in public places Inferred.

Firm-approved AI only

THE JD makes responsible AI use a duty (D9). The Global Code commits Deloitte to "responsible development and deployment of new technologies, including artificial intelligence" [S36] Confirmed. Deloitte UK's 2025 Transparency Report rates generative AI a "Very High" priority risk, with controls including "use-case approval" and "data governance" [S345] Confirmed. The firm's governance base is its "Trustworthy AI Framework" [S35] Confirmed. And in recruitment, candidates must read Deloitte's "Integrity & AI guidance" before the assessments [S17] Confirmed.

Timesheet integrity

"We record hours worked timely and accurately, and submit legitimate business-related expenses" [S36] Confirmed. This is not admin. Time and expense reporting made up 14% of ethics allegations at Deloitte UK in FY26 [S23] Confirmed. If a manager ever asks you to move hours to a different code or under-record them, that is a Code issue to raise, not a favour to do Inferred.

Figure 22 pulls the walls together: for each one, what may cross with the right process and what may not.

SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW (UNPROMPTED, IF THE MOMENT FITS)

"Because Deloitte audits some of the biggest UK companies, the consulting side often cannot work for them. About 96% of its non-audit revenue comes from companies it does not audit, and every engagement goes through a conflict check first. I would expect to make my own independence declarations from day one."

"The JD says firm-approved AI tools. To me that means client data stays inside approved systems, and I check every AI-assisted output before it reaches a client, because I am accountable for it."

"I see the timesheet as part of integrity. The firm bills on recorded time, so accurate hours protect the client and the firm."

DON'T SAY THIS

"Deloitte can sell anything to anyone because it is so big." It cannot: independence rules close off most consulting to listed audit clients [S39]. Also avoid naming Deloitte's internal AI tools for T&T, or its performance system, as if you know them. These are not public.

The team mapped: where TST sits and who leads it

Deloitte does not publish an organisation chart for T&T. What follows is reconstructed from service pages, press releases, leadership pages, the annual accounts and job postings. Each box in Figure 18 is coloured by how sure we are: green where a current primary page confirms it, amber where it rests on one source or a page that may be out of date, violet where it is our inference or unknown.

The legal frame, in three lines

Deloitte LLP is a limited liability partnership registered in England and Wales, number OC303675, at 1 New Street Square, London [S24][S407] Confirmed. From 1 June 2026 it combined with 14 other Deloitte member firms in Europe, the Middle East and Africa to form Deloitte EMEA; the old parent, Deloitte NSE LLP, ceased to be the parent [S24] Confirmed. A press summary says 16 participating firms [S33] Reported, so the count differs between sources. Deloitte EMEA is a member firm of Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL), which "do[es] not provide services to clients" [S407] Confirmed. Some job postings still carry old footer text naming Deloitte NSE LLP [S2]; the accounts show that changed on 1 June 2026 [S24].

Where TST sits

Follow the chain from the top. Deloitte UK has four businesses. TST sits inside Technology & Transformation, inside the Enterprise Technology & Performance offering, next to Finance Transformation, Supply Chain & Network Operations and the SAP, Oracle and ServiceNow practices [S12][S40][S41] Confirmed. Its UK Lead Partner is Matt Stallard, named on the TST service page [S41] Confirmed. TST's four market offerings, from THE JD, are Technology Operating Model; Enterprise Transformation & Agility; Technology Strategy, Vision and Architecture; and Technology Sourcing & Commercial Management [S2] Confirmed.

How the work splits: offering, industry and location

Every engagement sits at a crossing point of three things: an offering (what kind of work), an industry (whose sector) and a location (where the people sit). Experienced-hire titles show the grid directly, for example "Associate Director - Technology, Vision, Strategy & Architecture (Financial Services - Banking & Capital Markets)" [S49] Confirmed. The change team in Belfast lists the industries it serves: Consumer Business; TMT; ER&I; LSHC; Public Sector; Financial Services [S5] Confirmed.

The mechanism Inferred: offerings own skills, methods, software alliances and people (your People Leader sits in your offering). Industry and account teams own client relationships and sales. A large engagement draws people from several offerings. Your Resource Manager is how the grid assigns you to work.

Industry mix tells you where your first projects are most likely to be. UK revenue by industry in FY26 was: Financial Services £1,735m; Consumer £972m; Government and Public Services £679m (down from £761m in FY24); Technology, Media & Telecoms £632m; Energy, Resources & Industrials £535m; Life Sciences & Healthcare £235m; other £226m [S23] Confirmed. Financial services is about 35% of UK revenue Inferred (arithmetic), and the new T&T leader comes from insurance consulting [S27] Reported.

Why a central offering like TST exists

Without someone to frame the problem, a client buying technology change faces a tangle: separate conversations with platform specialists, cyber, data, HR systems and build teams, with nobody owning the overall answer or the business case. A strategy-led team sits in the middle, shapes the question with the client's leaders, and pulls in the right specialists Inferred. THE JD says TST teams "combine strategic thinking, advisory services, and cutting-edge technology capabilities" and work "with teams across our wider Technology and Transformation practice" [S2] Confirmed. Figure 19 shows the mechanism.

Delivery centres and offices

Not all T&T work happens in London or on client sites.

  • Belfast is "the premier local delivery centre for the whole of our UK firm, providing services across all our business areas" and "one of Deloitte's tech hubs" [S21] Confirmed. Most of the current early-careers consulting postings are in Belfast [S1].
  • Cardiff is "our ever-growing Delivery Centre", supporting client-facing colleagues "with everything from IT support to admin and more" [S20] Confirmed.
  • Bristol is "a tech hub" with "a rapidly growing group of creative engineers" [S20] Confirmed; Reading focuses on technology and telecoms as a "centre of excellence" [S20] Confirmed. Newcastle is a centre of excellence for audit, not consulting [S20].
  • Scotland: Edinburgh and Glasgow opened their roles first this cycle [S14]; Edinburgh hosts the current Risk & Controls Consulting graduate roles [S1].
  • New delivery centres. Deloitte says its new UK technology delivery centres were "fully operational in FY26" [S407] Confirmed. Their locations are not named in the release.
  • Offshore. Early-careers pages refer to "UK and offshore offices" [S13], and the UK group owns Deloitte India Services Limited [S24] Confirmed. Which offshore centres UK T&T uses is not confirmed on a primary UK page (gap). Postings say only "onshore and offshore" [S50][S51].

How a client request moves through the team

Figure 20 follows one piece of work from the first client conversation to the close. Two steps are easy to forget and matter most for the firm: the conflict and independence check before anything is agreed, and staffing, which is where you enter the story.

The scarce resource: your time

In a matrix firm, the thing two managers most often compete for is a good Analyst's week. Deloitte does not publish its staffing rules, so Figure 21 shows the usual pattern Inferred. The point for an interview is behavioural: when two managers both want you, you do not choose by yourself, and you do not hide the clash. You tell both of them, let the Resource Manager decide, and then commit.

How this compares with peers

A sourced, like-for-like comparison of Deloitte UK's T&T team with the consulting arms of PwC, EY, KPMG or Accenture in the UK is not available from the research for this Part. Their UK consulting revenue and structures were not read (gap). What can be said:

  • Deloitte calls its consulting arm "Technology & Transformation" globally, in line with its four-business model [S24][S34] Confirmed.
  • A trade analyst said Deloitte UK T&T growth in FY26 was "aligned with PwC UK's FY26 consulting sales rise" [S30] Reported.
  • Gartner ranked Deloitte the largest consulting services provider by revenue in 2025 [S33] Reported.
  • Big Four graduate training is being reshaped "as AI handles first-year data work" [S32] Reported (minor outlet).

Part 4 of this pack covers competitors in more depth. Do not make numeric peer comparisons from this Part.

What to take from this Part

  • Use the current names: four businesses; "Consulting" means T&T; TST sits in ET&P.
  • Most of an Analyst's first year is documents, analysis and coordination (D6, D8), with requirements work (D7) on delivery projects. Say so: it shows realism.
  • The business case (D4) links strategy to delivery. It is the thread through Figures 15 and 16.
  • Independence, conflicts, confidentiality, approved AI and honest timesheets are part of the job, not paperwork. You can say this unprompted.
  • Re-check the London postings from 5 October and choose one team, because you get one application a year.
SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW

"TST sits in Enterprise Technology & Performance inside T&T, which is Deloitte UK's largest business at about £1.75bn. What draws me is the span from the business case to implementation: the team can shape a decision with a CIO, then work with the SAP, Oracle or Workday teams to deliver it. As an Analyst I would expect most of my time to go on requirements, documents and programme tracking, and I would like to be the person whose RAID log and minutes people trust."

Part 2

The firm as a business, from the inside

How Deloitte UK earns a pound, who keeps it, who is protected from whom, and what has gone wrong. Read this once and you can talk about the firm the way a partner thinks about it, with the numbers and the dates.

Most candidates describe Deloitte from the careers website: big, global, "purpose-led". Interviewers hear that all day. This Part explains the firm as a business. It traces a client's fee from the invoice to a partner's profit share, shows the legal wiring that holds nearly 500,000 people under one brand, and lists the failures you should know before anyone asks. Every number has a source and a date. Where a number is our own arithmetic, it says so.

Two housekeeping points first, because they trip up almost everyone:

  • Deloitte's year ends on 31 May. "FY2026" means 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026 [S93] Confirmed. Results come out in late September.
  • "Deloitte UK" headline numbers include Switzerland. Deloitte's own footnote says: "All revenue numbers presented herein, unless otherwise noted, represent UK and Switzerland consolidated" [S407] Confirmed. So the £5.81bn headline is UK plus Switzerland. The UK on its own was £5,014m, and Switzerland £795m [S88] Confirmed.
£5.81bnRevenue FY2026, UK and Switzerland consolidated, +2% [S88][S407]
£5.01bnUK-only revenue FY2026 (the four UK businesses) [S88]
£899mDistributable profit FY2026, +14% (UK and Switzerland) [S84][S407]
£1.125mAverage profit per equity partner FY2026, up from £1.051m [S407]

A. The founding insight: an independent check on other people's numbers

William Welch Deloitte set up as an accountant in Basinghall Street, London, in 1845. He is described as the first person appointed as independent auditor of a public company, the Great Western Railway [S103] Reported. That is the founding idea, and it still runs the business: investors and lenders will put money into a company only if someone independent has checked the accounts. The auditor sells trust.

KEY TERM

Audit: an independent check that a company's published accounts are fair. The auditor signs an "opinion". Investors rely on it, so the auditor must be independent of the company it checks. That need for independence is the source of many of Deloitte's rules today (Section D).

How the name was built: a chain of mergers

DateWhat happenedSource
1845William Welch Deloitte opens his London practice.[S103] Reported
1952Merges with Haskins & Sells (US): Deloitte Haskins & Sells.[S103] Reported
1989Combines with Touche Ross in the US: Deloitte & Touche.[S103] Reported
1993International firm renamed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu. Tohmatsu was the Japanese partner firm.[S103] Reported
2002Arthur Andersen's UK practice joins Deloitte UK, after Andersen collapsed over the Enron scandal.[S103] Reported
10 Jan 2003Deloitte LLP, today's UK firm, is incorporated as a limited liability partnership.[S93] Confirmed
31 Mar 2003Deloitte abandons its plan to spin off consulting as "Braxton". It becomes the only Big Four firm to keep its consultancy.[S104] Reported
1 Jun 2026Deloitte LLP and its Swiss practice combine with 14 other member firms to form Deloitte EMEA.[S93] Confirmed

The decision that made today's firm: keeping consulting

In 2001 the US energy company Enron collapsed. Its auditor, Arthur Andersen, also earned large consulting fees, and regulators asked whether an auditor that sells consulting can stay tough on its client. The US passed the Sarbanes-Oxley Act in 2002, which tightened auditor independence. The other big accounting firms got rid of their consulting arms. Ernst & Young sold to Cap Gemini (2000). KPMG Consulting floated and became BearingPoint (2001). PwC Consulting was sold to IBM (2002) [S104] Reported.

Deloitte planned to do the same. In February 2002 it announced that Deloitte Consulting would be separated as a partner-owned firm called "Braxton". On 31 March 2003 it dropped the plan, citing a "tight credit market and the uncertain state of the economy" [S104] Reported. It committed to keep consulting "focused on nonaudit clients", in line with the new rules [S104]. Some clients were reported to have walked away during the uncertainty [S104] Reported.

So the choice was partly forced by market conditions, not a grand strategic vision. But its effect has been huge. In FY2025, consulting services were US$43.7bn of Deloitte's US$70.5bn global revenue, about 62% [S81] Confirmed. Gartner ranks Deloitte the number one consulting provider worldwide by revenue, for the eighth year running [S301] Confirmed. Deloitte has had more than 20 years to build a multidisciplinary firm while rivals rebuilt their consultancies from scratch. Part 3 explains why that structure works and what it costs; this Part sticks to how it makes money.

KEY TERM

Multidisciplinary firm: one firm that sells audit, tax, consulting and deal advice under one brand. The upside is breadth and steadier income across the economic cycle. The downside is constant policing of conflicts between audit clients and advisory work. See Part 3 for the full mechanism.

Purpose statement

Deloitte's stated purpose is "to make an impact that matters, for our clients, our people, and society" [S82] Confirmed (read on the Global Facts and Figures page, 4 October 2026). The UK audit business has its own: "Protecting the public interest and building trust and confidence in business" [S94] Confirmed (Audit Transparency Report 2025).

DON'T SAY THIS

"Deloitte has always been a consulting firm." It started as an audit firm, nearly gave consulting away in 2002-03, and kept it partly by accident of timing [S104]. Knowing that history shows you understand why audit independence rules still shape what consultants can sell.

SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW

"Deloitte is the only Big Four firm that kept its consultancy after Sarbanes-Oxley. It nearly spun it out as Braxton and pulled back in 2003. Today consulting is about 62% of global revenue, and Technology & Transformation alone was US$33.4bn in FY2025." [S104][S81]

B. How the firm makes money: from a client's fee to a partner's share

Deloitte UK is a partnership. That one fact explains most of its economics, so start there.

KEY TERM

Limited liability partnership (LLP): a business owned by its partners (legally called "members") rather than by shareholders. Partners share the profit. Unlike an old-style partnership, members are generally not personally liable for the firm's debts. Deloitte LLP is registered in England and Wales as OC303675 [S93][S407] Confirmed.

KEY TERM

Equity partner vs salaried partner: an equity partner owns a share of the firm, puts in capital and takes a share of profit. A salaried partner carries the partner title but is an employee on a salary and bonus. In FY2026 Deloitte UK averaged 799 equity partners and 654 salaried partners (full-time-equivalent averages, 1,453 in all) [S88] Confirmed.

The business model in one paragraph

Clients pay fees for work done by teams of people. The firm pays those people salaries, pays sub-contractors, and pays for offices, IT and its share of the global network. Whatever is left is profit, and it all belongs to the equity partners. There are no outside shareholders and no retained-earnings growth story. So the core question for the partnership every year is: how much fee income can a given number of partners generate, through how many staff, at what cost?

SAY THIS IN THE INTERVIEW

"The £5.81bn headline is UK and Switzerland consolidated. UK-only revenue was about £5.0bn, and T&T was the largest single business at £1.75bn, up 4% after a 10% fall the year before." [S88][S407][S89] Getting the Switzerland point right signals you read the release, not a headline.

Where each pound goes: the cost structure

Deloitte LLP files audited group accounts (audited by BDO LLP) at Companies House [S93] Confirmed. They show where the money goes. The percentages are our arithmetic on the reported figures.
